title: Agent brain: who takes each step

flows.name: Commit a change
flows.summary: P1–P4: a small working commit with the ticket id and the model, effort and harness it was made with.
steps: Slice the change into one coherent capability
Write the subject, the why, and the summary
Subject shape, ticket id, and the Model / Thinking-effort / Harness trailers
Install the commit-msg and pre-push hooks

flows.name: Spawn an agent
flows.summary: DS10 with P5–P6 and DS2–DS5: everything an agent needs before work, in one command that a resumed session runs again.
steps: Record the environment in the ledger before the first side effect
Claim host ports machine-wide; a resumed spawn keeps the ones it holds
Reuse the marked worktree, or restore it on the local branch, else origin's, else a new branch from the base; mark the registration
Copy .env without AWS credentials when git ignores it; install when the checkout or a lockfile is new
Reserve the Compose project name machine-wide on this Docker daemon, only when it is empty or already this environment's; bring it up
Declare persona, skills, tools, model, harness, effort

flows.name: Tear down an agent
flows.summary: DS11 with P7: after the merge, or on a canceled ticket, remove only what spawn created.
steps: Delete the remote branch at merge; leave the local branch to teardown only when that teardown will delete it
Merged, or canceled and run with --abandon
Check everything first: owner, spawn's mark, a clean worktree on its branch, the merge, the Compose reservation on a reachable, matching daemon
Remove the worktree with everything in it, ignored files included
Delete the local branch only when spawn created it, it merged, nothing holds it, and it is still at the checked tip
Bring down the reserved Compose project with its volumes and snapshot, then release the reservation, the ports, and the ledger entry
Close the Herdr tabs this agent opened (herdr-fanout)

flows.name: Raise a pull request
flows.summary: P8, P10, P11, P13: one PR per ticket, small, with a changelog line.
steps: Find the existing PR for the ticket before creating one
A CHANGELOG.md line is in the change
Fill the PR body from the template
Verify the change in the running app against its acceptance criteria
Exactly one Blast-radius line in the PR body's opening block, its reason naming no other grade
Open the PR ready, never as a draft
Decide how to split an oversized change
Write the changelog line under each affected surface's Unreleased, or Project's
Link the PR on the ticket; high or ticket-requested: hand the code-reviewer (model from review-models.json) the PR to review and merge, under its assignment name

flows.name: Review a pull request
flows.summary: P10, P14: adversarial review with inline findings and a submitted verdict.
steps: Rate each finding's severity and propose the fix
Post inline comments and a verdict opening with the Reviewer and Verdict lines
File a review issue in Linear per finding
Author fixes, replies with the commit, resolves the thread
Read the PR's CI status and act on it
Author hands the new head back to the same assignment until it approves; on a delivery assignment the reviewer merges on green CI, otherwise it only returns the verdict

flows.name: Merge a pull request
flows.summary: P12, P15, P17: a merge commit with the ticket id, when green and, for a high blast radius, approved; the author or the reviewer merges.
steps: Ready (not a draft), one graded blast radius, CI green, no outstanding change request, and approved when high or the ticket asks
Merge commit, never squash, ticket id in the message
Move the ticket to Merged with a status update

flows.name: Release a version
flows.summary: L1: one surface (backend, web, mobile) at a time: its semver, its changelog entry listing the tickets, a tag and a GitHub release.
steps: Decide that the release should go out
Pick the surface's semver bump from its Unreleased lines' impact
Rename the surface's Unreleased to the new version and date, and open a new empty one

flows.name: Take in a request
flows.summary: M1–M2: the request lands in Triage verbatim, then is classified.
steps: Record the prompt verbatim on a Triage issue
Classify kind, owning persona, scope, and size

flows.name: Move an issue and say why
flows.summary: M3, M5: every state change carries a structured status update.
steps: Is the move legal, and which states does it skip
Render the status update in the template's shape
Validate the Blocked block and its blocker type
Write the reason, evidence, and next action
Post the comment and change the state in Linear
Read back and quote the identifier

flows.name: Set up a team's workflow
flows.summary: Created once per team by the user.
steps: Create the missing workflow states in order

flows.name: Plan the work
flows.summary: Scope, milestones, issues, estimates, cycles.
steps: Decide scope and divide it into milestones and issues
Estimate effort on the team's scale
Create the project, milestones, issues, and relations
Settle the plan and the PRD; the user reviews only when asked

flows.name: Write a PRD
flows.summary: Idea to a phased PRD with an MVP first.
steps: Interview the user and refine the idea
Settle open questions; the user reviews only when asked

flows.name: Write HLD, LLD and ADRs
flows.summary: Design as code, settled with no open question; the user reviews only when asked.
steps: Decide the architecture and the contracts
Write the HLD, LLD, and ADRs
Documents sit where W9–W11 say and are in the index
Rendered HTML sits beside its Markdown
Settle open questions; the user reviews only when asked
User reviews an ADR for a one-way-door decision

flows.name: Implement a slice
flows.summary: Code and tests in the agent's own environment, one verified behavior per commit.
steps: Design the code and write it
Write the test behind each acceptance criterion
Run lint, type check, tests, and build
Start the service in its own Docker project and seed data

flows.name: Hold the coding standards
flows.summary: C1–C23 split into what a linter can see and what needs a reader.
steps: Strict types, no any, linter and type checker present
No edits to generated or vendor files
No inline clock or randomness in business modules
No secrets in source or fixtures
Separate API, domain, and DB models; errors as domain objects
Business validation only at the edges

flows.name: Debug a failure
flows.summary: Reproduce, localise, fix, guard.
steps: Localise the cause and choose the fix

flows.name: Audit security
flows.summary: Never holds a PR (P9).
steps: Scan for secrets and vulnerable dependencies
Reason about trust boundaries and abuse cases

flows.name: Audit web performance
flows.summary: Measured numbers only.

flows.name: Verify a milestone
flows.summary: Independent end-to-end and concurrency verification.
steps: Design the end-to-end and race scenarios
File a bug issue per failure

flows.name: Double-pass review of a brain PR
flows.summary: AGENTS.md gate: two independent reviewers, then a synthesis, on the models in review-models.json.
steps: Start both reviewers on the same revision with the models in review-models.json
Check that both reviews and the synthesis cover the final revision

flows.name: Start a session
flows.summary: /brain: one persona, declared.
steps: Pick a persona for the task
Fetch the skills its table names for the activity
Declare persona, skills, tools, model, harness, effort

flows.name: Orchestrate worker sessions
flows.summary: /orchestrator: one session per project routes each request to a new, resumed, or running worker in its own Herdr tab and never does the work.
steps: Claim the project's one orchestrator in the record and reconcile it with live tabs
Rank recorded sessions against the request
Decide new, resume, or send; split a mixed request; judge staleness
Launch, resume, or restart the worker under its session id with hooks and held prompts; message a live one
Retry a failed resume or give the session a new conversation (relaunch)
Record the decision and its reason, then its outcome once the route has run
Answer a trust or login prompt in a new worker's tab
Hold prompts until each is accepted, then deliver the rest
Settle a prompt of unknown delivery after checking the worker (resend or drop)
Record every worker prompt, compaction, and /clear
Worker keeps its summary, ticket, worktree, and resolution current
Close a settled worker's tab, keeping its record
Say whether work is finished when the worker has not

flows.name: Check the brain
flows.summary: Anatomies, links, commands, evals, and the persona table.
steps: Persona anatomy, manifest, and the persona table
Review models are config; no AGENTS.md names a model
Every convention rule ID is cited by a flow step

flows.name: Build and install the brain
flows.summary: manifest.json to build/ to a project.
steps: Pull the brain into a repository
Decide which skills and personas the brain contains

flows.name: Turn a learning into a rule
flows.summary: LEARNINGS.md notes become changes here.
steps: Record the override, correction, or gap when it happens
Decide that a note recurs enough to change a rule
Approve the change to the brain

flows.name: Session hooks
flows.summary: Hooks that run without a model.
steps: Inject the meta-skill at session start (the hook script exists but no host registers it)
Cache source reads before and after

flows.name: Development-session tracing
flows.summary: Pi and Claude sessions in an opted-in project become Langfuse observations: bounded local state, then a flushed outbox.
steps: Admit a checkpoint within the 2,048-file / 32 MiB adapter cap, reclaiming expired unreferenced state first
At the cap, quarantine stale pre-ticket batches (never sent, never read); nothing else moves, and nothing moves when a reference is unknown
Record the quarantine or the refusal in health, outside the ordinary cap
Flush up to 32 queued records and wait for every batch reply before shutting the exporter down
Read health and delivery with context status

flows.name: Run a dev machine
flows.summary: EC2 Spot machines for developers.
steps: Survive a Spot reclaim and relaunch

flows.name: Build iOS on EAS
flows.summary: DS16: only with explicit permission.
steps: Count free builds, queue, build, report
Decide to wait or build elsewhere when the budget is spent

flows.name: Instrument what ships
flows.summary: O1–O8: structured logs and RED metrics for every new boundary.
steps: Decide which metrics and log events matter
Bounded labels and no PII or secrets in logs
Provision dashboards and alerts at the planned milestone

flows.name: Trace a Claude Code session
flows.summary: Each hook event is processed in native order by a capped work process; tracing may drop data but never slows or blocks the session.
steps: Hook entrypoint runs discovery in a child process group, kills it past the cap, and passes its deadline down
Event work process applies the event and reads a budgeted transcript slice; it ends by the passed deadline with its process group
One background uploader delivers captured records to Langfuse; its lifetime cap kills its process group
